# TA2726

(REVISE: FOLLOW THE FLOW OF THE SLIDE DECK, FOR IT IS REFINED)

We'll start the TA2726 learning process by searching for TA2726 indicators from ProofPoint's Emerging Threats. Search for it using the link below.
[https://community.emergingthreats.net/search?q=TA2726%20order%3Alatest](https://community.emergingthreats.net/search?q=TA2726%20order%3Alatest)

I'm using the results below. You can click the link below to follow along, or, you can use something newer (or older). Keep in mind that sometimes the newer stuff might not have as many scans in urlscan, so it is always easier to use something that has been flagged for a while. If the indicators you use don't work, work your way backwards to something older.

https://community.emergingthreats.net/t/ruleset-update-summary-2025-09-30-v11027/3066

![](data:image/png;base64,)

From the snip above, we can see that quietshalecompany[.]com is reported as a TA2726 TDS domain. We will use that indicator.

Go to [virustotal.com](http://virustotal.com) and search the domain. If you’re following along, you can use this link directly: [https://www.virustotal.com/gui/domain/quietshalecompany.com/detection](https://www.virustotal.com/gui/domain/quietshalecompany.com/detection)

Observe the scoring. At the point in time when I took this snip, 16/95 security vendors flagged this domain as malicious.
  
![](data:image/png;base64,)

Go to the Community tab and observe the comments. Make a mental note of it. We will use this as a validation method. You can use the following link to go there directly: [https://www.virustotal.com/gui/domain/quietshalecompany.com/community](https://www.virustotal.com/gui/domain/quietshalecompany.com/community)

![](data:image/png;base64,)
  
Next go to the Relations tab. [https://www.virustotal.com/gui/domain/quietshalecompany.com/relations](https://www.virustotal.com/gui/domain/quietshalecompany.com/relations)

![](data:image/png;base64,)  

Click the most recent IP.

If you’re following along, you’d be here: [https://www.virustotal.com/gui/ip-address/144.31.193.106](https://www.virustotal.com/gui/ip-address/144.31.193.106)
  
![](data:image/png;base64,)

Review the comments, make a mental note, and note the similar comments.

![](data:image/png;base64,) 

Click the Relations tab.

![](data:image/png;base64,) 

Note the additional domains. Click one of them to view the VirusTotal page for it.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Next, you’ll want to click the link for the Virustotal page for the domain. For me, it’s that javascriptbasics[.]com link that’s selected.

![](data:image/png;base64,) 

Note the analysis, then check the comments.

![](data:image/png;base64,)
  
Check if the community is also stating that this domain matches other comments. In my example, it does. JaffaCakes118 reports that it’s listed in THREATfox with the malware family “FAKEUPDATES” (also known as SocGholish).

**CHECKPOINT:**

You used an intelligence lead (the ProofPoint Ruleset Update Summary) and processed it to find additional adversary infrastructure.

In a way, you are validating the infrastructure using external validation. For this to work, you need to trust the community making those comments. TA2726 is known for their web injects. They inject malicious code into compromised websites. We can validate the infrastructure first hand by searching for the suspected domains in urlscan.

[https://urlscan.io](https://urlscan.io)

Or, you can view the same search here: [https://urlscan.io/search/#quietshalecompany.com](https://urlscan.io/search/#quietshalecompany.com)
  
![](data:image/png;base64,)
  
I analyze the result here: [https://urlscan.io/result/0199d50e-e224-7546-9b97-168d22c41a22/](https://urlscan.io/result/0199d50e-e224-7546-9b97-168d22c41a22/)

Take note of the basic urlscan layout. Click around to understand the options. Return here when you're done.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Go to the HTTP tab. It lists the requests for each resource.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Find the quietshale domain (or whatever domain you’re checking). Take notice how it uses a weird string in the request URL (in my example it’s jRDYtEaPzW5Hl2WPQbTOsHxgMjg-kf47wbu1NtVADRC).

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Next, repeat the process with the additional infrastructure. For me, I will search urlscan for “javascriptbasics[.]com”, and I will compare the request URLs.

[https://urlscan.io/search/#javascriptbasics.com](https://urlscan.io/search/#javascriptbasics.com)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

[http://urlscan.io/result/0199d4c1-a59b-754d-97a3-97de08b1f9d2/](http://urlscan.io/result/0199d4c1-a59b-754d-97a3-97de08b1f9d2/)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

[https://urlscan.io/result/0199d4c1-a59b-754d-97a3-97de08b1f9d2/#transactions](https://urlscan.io/result/0199d4c1-a59b-754d-97a3-97de08b1f9d2/#transactions)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

I observe the scan task for flyingmedicalservice[.]org requests a long strange string (qL47K60lP5cVUktyGfwp1Xbnu0BHaOcVL70kiD1KbbD) from the suspected TA2726 domain javascriptbasics[.]com.

**CHECKPOINT:** You have just validated the pivot using first-hand observations.

First-hand validations have more value because it relies on your analysis. External validations could introduce the risk of a bad assessment. With time, you will gain confidence in external sources.

Note: We did not discuss an in-depth analysis on the malware delivery. This is just a cursory glance into simple pivot concepts.

**Summary**

In this section, you’ve learned how to use Proofpoint’s Community Ruleset as an intelligence lead. You processed the lead and identified additional adversary infrastructure. You validated the pivot using external sources (VirusTotal comments). You also validated the pivot using first-hand observations (urlscan observations).
